note: v2152: A cross-family review of v2150 answered that its own claim, one source now and both callers use it, was already false. It was right: counter_ledger.resolve_all still walked the same found-intersect-notFound set with its own copy of the inclusion rule, and the chain tests reach the resolver through it, so the next edit to who counts as contested had two places to miss. derive_contested now delegates to resolve_all outright. Three more from the same review, each reproduced first: an empty notFoundSeen bucket minted a contradiction from no evidence because membership was tested on the KEY and merge_proposals creates keys before it appends; notFoundDatable compared two different populations, names in notFound against KEYS in notFoundSeen, so a receipt for an unrelated name could declare every reading orderable; and the per-name resolver swallow silently rebuilt the padded count when counter_ledger could not be imported, which looked identical to a measured answer. resolverOk is published and ok goes None rather than False.
